title: Leak repair
description: Dripping, spraying or soaking through the ceiling. Found, fixed and pressure-tested the same day.
imageAlt: A plumber's hands soldering a new copper elbow under a bathroom vanity, a small blue flame at the joint.
content:
Most leaks we see come from three places: a braided supply line that has given up, a pinhole in copper that is older than the house's second owner, or a joint that was never quite right. Each one is a short job once it is found. Finding it is the part we are good at.

What the visit includes

  • Shutting off and draining the affected line so nothing else gets wet
  • A moisture meter and, behind walls, a thermal camera before we cut anything
  • Replacing the failed section in copper or PEX to match what you have
  • A pressure test, and a photo of the finished repair for your records

If it is behind a wall

We open the smallest hole that gets the job done, cut it square so a drywaller can patch it in an hour, and tell you the price of the repair before we open anything.

title: Drain cleaning
description: Kitchen, bath, laundry or the main line. Cleared with a cable or jetter, camera-checked on request.
imageAlt: A plumber in blue gloves feeding a drain cable into a floor drain in a bright white laundry room.
content:
One slow sink is a local clog and a quick job. Two fixtures backing up at once, or a gurgle in the tub when the washer drains, points to the main line. We will tell you which on the phone, so the right machine comes on the van.

How we clear it

  • A hand cable for sinks, tubs and showers, from the trap or the nearest cleanout
  • A drum machine or hydro-jetter for the main line and anything with roots
  • Ten minutes of running water afterwards to prove it drains
  • A camera inspection on request, with the recording emailed to you

Keeping it clear

If the same line keeps clogging, the camera usually shows why: a belly in the pipe, a root intrusion, or a bad joint. We quote the permanent fix in writing, and you decide when.

title: Water heaters
description: Tank and tankless, gas and electric. Repaired from the van or replaced with the old one hauled away.
imageAlt: A plumber checking the gas valve on a newly installed white tank water heater with fresh copper and brass pipework.
content:
A water heater with no hot water is usually a part, not a new heater. We carry thermocouples, igniters, elements and thermostats for the common makes, so most repairs are done on the first visit.

When it is time to replace

  • The tank itself is leaking, which no part can fix
  • It is past twelve years and the repair costs more than a third of a new one
  • You are moving to tankless and want the gas line and venting done properly

What a replacement includes

The heater, a new shutoff, expansion tank and flex lines, the permit and inspection, and hauling the old unit away. Most swaps are done in half a day, and you have hot water again before dinner.

title: Toilets & faucets
description: Running, rocking, dripping or just dated. Repaired or replaced, your fixture or ours.
imageAlt: A plumber installing a new chrome faucet on a white basin in a bathroom with white subway tile.
content:
A running toilet can waste two hundred gallons a day, and a dripping faucet adds up on the bill just as quietly. Both are quick fixes. Replacing a fixture you are tired of looking at is barely longer.

What we do

  • Toilet tank rebuilds: flapper, fill valve and flush valve
  • Wax seals and flanges for a toilet that rocks or smells
  • Faucet cartridges, or a new faucet fitted and tested
  • Shutoff valves and supply lines replaced while we are under there

Bought your own?

Fine by us. We fit customer-supplied fixtures at the same flat price, and our one-year guarantee covers the installation.

title: Repiping
description: Old galvanized or polybutylene pipe replaced with PEX, a room at a time, drywall patched.
imageAlt: New red and blue PEX water lines running neatly through basement joists to a brass manifold with blue shutoff valves.
content:
If your house was built before 1960, there is a fair chance the water still runs through galvanized steel that has narrowed with rust. Weak pressure, brown water after a trip away, and one leak after another are the signs.

How a repipe works

  • A walk-through and a written, fixed quote, usually the same week
  • New PEX runs to a manifold, so every fixture gets its own shutoff
  • Water back on at the end of every working day
  • Openings patched and ready for paint when we leave

Living through it

Most houses take two to four days. We work a room at a time, cover floors and furniture, and clean up every evening. You stay home the whole time.

title: Emergency call-outs
description: Burst pipes, sewer backups, no water at all. Answered 24/7, and nights cost the same as days.
imageAlt: A white plumbing van parked on a leafy street while a plumber carries a toolbox up the front path of a house.
content:
When water is coming through the ceiling, you need a person on the phone and a plumber at the door. A real dispatcher answers our emergency line at any hour and tells you the arrival time before you hang up.

Until we get there

  • Turn off the main shutoff, usually where the water line enters the basement or crawlspace
  • If water is near outlets or the panel, switch off that circuit
  • Open a faucet on the lowest floor to drain the lines
  • Take photos for your insurer before you start mopping

What it costs

The same $59 visit and the same flat prices as a weekday. We do not charge an after-hours rate, a holiday rate, or a call-out rate. We never have.
